trig-functions-12-pyq#25.basis: DEFECTIVE AS PRINTED — the board's own misprint, transcribed faithfully. The March 2022 paper prints \(c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} = ac\). Read literally that asserts two things at once, \(c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\) and \(a^{2} + b^{2} = ac\). Combining them gives \(c^{2} = ac\), hence \(c = a\); substituting back, \(a^{2} + b^{2} = a \cdot a = a^{2}\), forcing \(b = 0\). No such triangle exists and \(\angle B\) is undefined, so as printed no option can be correct. The intended condition is \(c^{2} + a^{2} - b^{2} = ac\): the SAME question in the March 2023 paper prints it that way, the textbook carries it that way, and it yields \(\angle B = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\), which is one of the four printed options. Preserved rather than repaired, per the PYQ-fidelity convention.
